title: "Styling with CSS (R)"
format:
  html:
    code-tools: true
    include-in-header: ../assets/amber-viewer.html
filters:
  - path: ../_filters/show-source.lua
    at: pre-ast

panzoom:
  css-class: plum-viewer
---

The viewer styled with CSS. `css-class`, in the YAML header, adds a class to the
viewer, and the rules below use it to set the viewer colors (plum, with pink
links), draw a line along the top of the caption band, and make the caption
larger and italic.

```yaml
---
panzoom:
  css-class: plum-viewer
---
```

The rules apply only to a viewer with that class, so other pages keep the
default viewer even if they load the same rules. A single
[image](#sec-class-for-one-image) or [code cell](#sec-class-for-one-cell) can
add a class of its own, which applies while that image is open.

The rules are in a raw HTML block on this page. The same block works in any
Quarto document:

````markdown {.show-source}
```{=html}
<style>
.plum-viewer {
  --panzoom-backdrop: rgba(60, 20, 70, 0.9);
  --panzoom-panel-bg: #2d1236;
  --panzoom-panel-fg: #f3e8f7;
  --panzoom-link: #ffb3d9;
}
.plum-viewer .panzoom-panel {
  border-top: 4px solid #d58cf0;
}
.plum-viewer .panzoom-caption {
  font-size: 1.15rem;
  font-style: italic;
}
.sea-viewer {
  --panzoom-backdrop: rgba(10, 50, 60, 0.9);
  --panzoom-panel-bg: #0f3640;
  --panzoom-panel-fg: #e0f4f7;
  --panzoom-link: #7fe0d0;
}
.sea-viewer .panzoom-panel {
  border-top-color: #4fc3c9;
}
.sea-viewer .panzoom-caption {
  font-style: normal;
}
</style>
```
````

The same rules can also go in a stylesheet file, or straight into the HTML
header, each set in the YAML header:

```yaml
---
format:
  html:
    css: viewer.css   # a file holding the rules above
---
```

```yaml
---
format:
  html:
    include-in-header:
      text: |
        <style>
        .plum-viewer { --panzoom-backdrop: rgba(60, 20, 70, 0.9); }
        </style>
---
```

A theme's `.scss` file works too. Rules on the viewer's parts start with the
viewer's class, as above, so they win over the defaults. The parts are
`.panzoom-panel` (the band or side panel around the caption, description, and
hint), `.panzoom-caption`, `.panzoom-description`, `.panzoom-hint`,
`.panzoom-close`, `.panzoom-prev`, `.panzoom-next`, and `.panzoom-counter`.

For a whole site, put `css-class` (or any option) under `format: html:` in
`_quarto.yml`. A top-level `panzoom:` there is replaced, not merged, by a page's
own `panzoom:` options.

## Markdown image {expect-open="panzoom" expect-class="plum-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(60, 20, 70, 0.9)" expect-band="rgb(45, 18, 54)"}

A markdown image with `.panzoom`. It opens with the plum viewer from the rules
above, with a line along the top of the caption band and a larger, italic
caption, and the link in its caption is pink.

```markdown {.show-source}
![Edgartown Lighthouse, Martha's Vineyard ([photo](https://unsplash.com/photos/f59MyOfLpi8)).](../images/mv-2.jpg){.panzoom fig-alt="A white lighthouse against a blue sky"}
```

## Class for one image {#sec-class-for-one-image expect-open="panzoom" expect-class="sea-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(10, 50, 60, 0.9)" expect-band="rgb(15, 54, 64)"}

A markdown image with `.panzoom` and a class of its own,
`css-class="sea-viewer"`. It opens with the dark teal `.sea-viewer` rules, a
teal line along the top of the caption band, and an upright caption, and the
link in its caption is teal. The `plum-viewer` class set under the `panzoom:`
option in the YAML header stays on the viewer too, so the `.sea-viewer` rules
come after the `.plum-viewer` ones to win over them.

```markdown {.show-source}
![A gingerbread cottage in Oak Bluffs, Martha's Vineyard ([photo](https://unsplash.com/photos/HQEtvlNzUyA)).](../images/mv-3.jpg){.panzoom css-class="sea-viewer" fig-alt="A shingled gingerbread cottage with pink and green trim, behind a garden path"}
```

## Code cell {expect-open="panzoom" expect-class="plum-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(60, 20, 70, 0.9)" expect-band="rgb(45, 18, 54)"}

An R cell with `#| panzoom: true`. It opens with the plum viewer set under the
`panzoom:` option in the YAML header.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of vapor pressure rising steeply with temperature"
#| fig-cap: "Vapor pressure of mercury against temperature."

plot(pressure, type = "b", pch = 19)
```

## Class for one cell {#sec-class-for-one-cell expect-open="panzoom" expect-class="sea-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(10, 50, 60, 0.9)" expect-band="rgb(15, 54, 64)"}

An R cell with `css-class: sea-viewer` under the `panzoom` cell option. It opens
with the teal viewer.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   css-class: sea-viewer
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of stopping distance against speed for 50 cars"
#| fig-cap: "Stopping distance against speed for 50 cars."

plot(cars, pch = 19)
```

## Gallery with mixed classes {expect-open="panzoom" expect-steps="true" expect-class="sea-viewer; plum-viewer; sea-viewer" expect-no-class="; sea-viewer;" expect-overlay="rgba(10, 50, 60, 0.9); rgba(60, 20, 70, 0.9); rgba(10, 50, 60, 0.9)"}

A gallery of three images, the first and last with `css-class="sea-viewer"`.
Each image has its class only while it is open, so the first and last show the
teal viewer and the middle one the plum viewer, whichever way it is reached.

```markdown {.show-source}
![Sunset at Chilmark Beach, Martha's Vineyard.](../images/mv-0.jpg){.panzoom group="mixed" css-class="sea-viewer" fig-alt="Sunset over a sandy beach, with a tall rock stack against the sun"}

![Waves breaking below the clay cliffs at Aquinnah, Martha's Vineyard.](../images/mv-1.jpg){.panzoom group="mixed" fig-alt="Waves breaking below grassy clay cliffs at Aquinnah"}

![A sailboat off Edgartown, Martha's Vineyard.](../images/mv-4.jpg){.panzoom group="mixed" css-class="sea-viewer" fig-alt="A sailboat with a flag-striped sail off a sandy beach"}
```

## Margin image {expect-open="panzoom" expect-class="plum-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(60, 20, 70, 0.9)" expect-band="rgb(45, 18, 54)"}

A markdown image with `.panzoom` in the margin. It opens with the plum viewer
set under the `panzoom:` option in the YAML header.

```markdown {.show-source}
![A gingerbread cottage in Oak Bluffs, Martha's Vineyard.](../images/mv-3.jpg){.panzoom .column-margin fig-alt="A shingled gingerbread cottage with pink and green trim, behind a garden path"}
```

## Class from a file {expect-open="panzoom" expect-class="amber-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(40, 25, 5, 0.92)" expect-band="rgb(58, 37, 8)"}

A markdown image with `.panzoom` and `css-class="amber-viewer"`. The rules for
that class are in a file, `assets/amber-viewer.html` in the panzoom repository,
which the YAML header includes. It opens with an amber viewer, an amber line
along the top of the caption band, and an upright caption, and the link in its
caption is gold.

```yaml
---
format:
  html:
    include-in-header: ../assets/amber-viewer.html
---
```

The file holds a `<style>` block. Included in the header, its rules come before
the page's own, so each starts with `.panzoom-overlay` too, to win over the
`.plum-viewer` rules above:

```css
.panzoom-overlay.amber-viewer {
  --panzoom-backdrop: rgba(40, 25, 5, 0.92);
  --panzoom-panel-bg: #3a2508;
  --panzoom-panel-fg: #fdf0d8;
  --panzoom-link: #ffc966;
}
```

```markdown {.show-source}
![A sailboat off Edgartown, Martha's Vineyard ([photo](https://unsplash.com/photos/IiLiz7XpQpI)).](../images/mv-4.jpg){.panzoom css-class="amber-viewer" fig-alt="A sailboat with a flag-striped sail off a sandy beach"}
```
